changes.after: Combine sorting rules so a second rule breaks ties in the first.

before: compareBy<String> { it.length } creates a Comparator ordered by string length; the explicit type argument says the elements are Strings. thenBy { it } compares the full String only when lengths tie. it is the implicit single lambda parameter.
Expected output or behavior: [ox, ant, bee]. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Add a second two-letter word and trace comparisons before and after reversal. You may trace it without a Kotlin compiler; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: A comparator is a rule for deciding which value comes first. `compareBy<String> { it.length }` compares the lengths of Strings. Shorter text comes before longer text.

The call `thenBy { it }` breaks a tie by comparing the text itself. For these lowercase words, that gives alphabetical order. The function sortedWith uses the combined rule to build a sorted list without changing the source list.
The screen shows `[ox, ant, bee]`. Ox is shortest. Ant and bee tie in length, so their text order puts ant first.
Calling `reversed()` on the whole comparator reverses both rules. Longer text comes first, and equal-length words use the opposite text order.
